problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)={e}^{x}$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=4{y}^{2}-8{e}^{x}y+4{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}
$$

 

find the general solution of the equation.
worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}=4{y}^{2}-8{e}^{x}y+4{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x},
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=4,\,b(x)=-8{e}^{x},\,c(x)=4{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)={e}^{x}.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)={e}^{x}$, we have

$$
y=z+{e}^{x}\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+{e}^{x}.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+{e}^{x}=4(z+{e}^{x})^{2}-8{e}^{x}(z+{e}^{x})+4{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}.
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+{e}^{x} & =4({e}^{2x}+2{e}^{x}z+{z}^{2})-8{e}^{x}z-8{e}^{2x}+4{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x} \\ {z}^{′}+{e}^{x} & =4{z}^{2}+{e}^{x} \\ {z}^{′} & =4{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =4{z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =4 \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 4\,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int 4\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & =4x+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{4x+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-{e}^{x}$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{4x+C} \\ y-{e}^{x} & =-\frac{1}{4x+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{4x+C}+{e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}-\frac{1}{4x+C}\end{aligned}
$$
